title: Finance and Prudential Essentials for Directors of Regulated Firms
summary: An eight-module programme giving non-financial directors the confidence to read a regulated firm's accounts, capital and liquidity position, and to challenge the CFO.
intro: This training programme equips non-executive directors without a finance background to read the numbers of a regulated firm with confidence: understanding financial statements, capital and liquidity, regulatory returns and plans, and challenging the finance function effectively.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give directors without an accounting or finance background a practical, jargon-free understanding of the financial and prudential position of regulated firms, and how to see the numbers the way a supervisor does. Participants leave able to read financial statements and regulatory returns, interpret capital, liquidity and stress test results, and put informed questions to the CFO and auditors.
sections.What It Covers: Financial statements of regulated firms, key ratios and performance measures, capital and liquidity adequacy, regulatory returns, internal capital and liquidity assessments, budgets and business plans, audit and accounting judgements, valuation, stress testing and reverse stress testing, and the questions directors should ask the CFO.
Intended Audience: Non-executive and independent directors without a finance or accounting background
Chairs and members of board committees other than audit, and newly appointed directors
Executive directors and senior managers from non-finance functions who sign off plans or returns
Learning Objectives: Explain how the financial statements of different types of regulated firm fit together
Interpret key ratios for profitability, capital, liquidity and efficiency
Assess capital and liquidity adequacy and the firm's internal assessments of both
Challenge budgets, business plans and the assumptions behind them
Evaluate audit findings, accounting judgements, valuations and stress test results
Use a structured question set to hold the CFO and finance function to account
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about two hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a two-day programme or as a series of board briefing sessions. Each module combines a short briefing with worked examples and a board question set, and modules can be selected or tailored to the firm's sector and business model.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No accounting or finance qualification is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, The Basel Framework (consolidated Basel III standards)
Basel Committee, Principles for Sound Liquidity Risk Management and Supervision (2008)
IOSCO, Principles for the Valuation of Collective Investment Schemes (2013)

modules.title: Reading the Financial Statements of a Regulated Firm
modules.summary: Plain-language guide to the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement, and how they look different for banks, investment firms, payment firms, fund managers and insurers.
objectives: Explain how the three primary statements connect
Recognise the distinctive features of different regulated business models
Identify the lines in the accounts that matter most to supervisors
syllabus: Income statement, balance sheet and cash flow: how they fit together
Business model differences: lending, dealing, payments, asset management and insurance
Client money and assets: why they sit apart from the balance sheet
Notes to the accounts: where the important information hides

modules.title: Key Ratios and Performance Measures
modules.summary: The ratios and measures that tell directors whether the firm is profitable, efficient and sustainable, and how to spot when headline numbers flatter the position.
objectives: Interpret profitability, efficiency and concentration measures
Compare performance over time and against peers
Identify warning signs behind apparently healthy figures
syllabus: Margins, return on equity, cost-income ratio and revenue concentration
Recurring versus one-off income and quality of earnings
Trend analysis and peer comparison
Red flags: rapid growth, related parties and unexplained movements

modules.title: Capital and Liquidity Adequacy
modules.summary: Why regulated firms must hold capital and liquid assets, how requirements are set and measured, and how directors judge whether headroom is sufficient.
objectives: Explain the purpose of capital and liquidity requirements in plain language
Interpret capital and liquidity ratios, buffers and headroom
Assess whether management actions and triggers are credible
syllabus: Own funds, capital quality and deductions
Risk-based, fixed-overhead and activity-based capital requirements
Liquidity requirements, buffers and funding concentration
Early warning indicators, recovery triggers and management actions

modules.title: Regulatory Returns and Internal Capital and Liquidity Assessments
modules.summary: What firms report to the authority, how directors gain comfort over its accuracy, and what a good internal assessment of capital and liquidity needs looks like.
objectives: Explain the main regulatory returns and the board's responsibility for them
Evaluate the quality of the firm's internal capital and liquidity assessment
Identify common weaknesses that supervisors challenge
syllabus: Regulatory reporting: content, frequency, controls and sign-off
Internal assessments of capital and liquidity: purpose, structure and board ownership
Wind-down planning and the cost of an orderly exit
Common supervisory findings on returns and internal assessments

modules.title: Budgets, Business Plans and Forecasts
modules.summary: How to challenge budgets, business plans and forecasts, test the assumptions behind them, and link plans to capital, liquidity and risk appetite.
objectives: Test the assumptions underlying budgets and business plans
Link business plans to capital, liquidity and risk appetite
Monitor performance against plan and respond to variances
syllabus: Anatomy of a business plan: revenue drivers, costs and investment
Testing assumptions: sensitivity, downside cases and optimism bias
Capital and liquidity implications of growth and new business
Variance analysis and reforecasting

modules.title: Audit, Accounting Judgements and Valuation
modules.summary: Where the numbers depend on judgement, from provisions and impairments to the valuation of hard-to-price assets, and how directors use the auditors to gain assurance.
objectives: Identify significant accounting judgements and estimates
Assess valuation approaches for illiquid and complex assets
Engage effectively with external and internal auditors
syllabus: Provisions, impairments, expected credit losses and revenue recognition
Valuation hierarchies, models and independent price verification
Reading the audit report, key audit matters and management letters
The board's relationship with the auditors and the audit committee

modules.title: Stress Testing and Reverse Stress Testing
modules.summary: How stress tests and reverse stress tests show the firm's vulnerabilities, how to judge whether scenarios are severe enough, and how results should shape board decisions.
objectives: Explain how stress and reverse stress tests are built
Challenge scenario severity, assumptions and management actions
Use stress test results in strategy, capital and risk appetite decisions
syllabus: Scenario design: idiosyncratic, market-wide and combined stresses
Reverse stress testing: what would make the business model fail
Plausibility of management actions under stress
Integrating results into planning, capital and recovery decisions

modules.title: Holding the Finance Function to Account
modules.summary: Brings the programme together into a board question set for the CFO, auditors and finance function, and a practical plan for improving the board's financial oversight.
objectives: Assess the capability and independence of the finance function
Specify the financial and prudential information the board needs
Produce a personal and board action plan for financial oversight
syllabus: Questions to ask the CFO: performance, capital, liquidity and judgements
Board financial and prudential management information
Seeing the numbers the way a supervisor does
Workshop: reviewing a board finance pack and agreeing actions

related.title: Board Effectiveness: Dynamics and Decision-Making
related.summary: A ten-module programme helping boards strengthen their dynamics, information and decision-making, and evidence effective oversight to supervisors.

related.title: Culture, Conduct and Accountability for Boards
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving boards the tools to shape and oversee culture, align incentives, hold individuals to account and evidence oversight to regulators.

related.title: Effective Governance for Boards and Directors
related.summary: A twelve-module programme covering the standards expected of individual directors and the practices that make a board effective, for regulated firms, fund boards and management companies.

related.title: Geopolitical and Emerging Risks for Boards
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping boards identify, debate and prepare for geopolitical and emerging risks, ending with a facilitated board scenario exercise.

related.title: Group Governance and Cross-Border Operations
related.summary: A nine-module programme helping boards and senior managers of cross-border groups balance group direction with local accountability, oversee intragroup arrangements and deal with multiple supervisors.

related.title: Induction for Directors of Regulated Firms
related.summary: A ten-module induction giving new directors of regulated firms the grounding to discharge their duties, understand supervisory expectations and oversee the firm's risks.
